note: [agent-bulk] numucc_em, 111 segments, 21 showers. VERTEX: event_half_span_cm 206.5, so I judged the vertex off the --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt100222) and NOT off the native sweep. At 60 cm the blue star sits on a clean kink where a curving track arrives from one side and a second prong leaves the other way; it is where the charge converges. Not a vertex failure. VERDICT SHOWER 113236 (2498.2 MeV, 69 segments, pdg 11, len 632.1, start ON the main vertex): OVER-CLUSTERED, on three independent grounds. (1) It swallows a straight minimum-ionising stem: 14003 is a SINGLE 110.3 cm segment tagged pdg 13, taken by pass4_proximity at 38.4 cm / 4.3 deg. 110 cm is about 8 radiation lengths - no electron survives that as one straight unbranched segment, and on a numucc event a 110 cm MIP-tagged track is the muon or a charged pion, not shower spray. I marked it OUT, and it is a STRONG mark, not a marginal one. (2) The yellow set spans two directions: on shw113236-az-055-el+65 it forks about 40 cm above the X into a long straight narrow track running one way and a large branching EM fan running the other, and BOTH carry the member halo. (3) The acceptance plot is the corroboration the brief asks for and it is emphatic: the members run out to 153.7 cm at up to 31.7 deg (member_span read back from the saved record; the circles that continue to ~190 cm in the same angular band are NON-members), with about forty of them piled at 100-155 cm and 12-18 deg - the entire cluster-108 fan, pulled in by pass3_cluster_map - while the pass-1 box allows only 5 deg beyond 130 cm. At 150 cm, 18 deg is 46 cm off-axis, four to five Moliere radii, which is not the lateral profile of one EM shower however energetic. What I did NOT resolve, and why the confidence is likely rather than certain: I cannot say whether the cluster-108 fan (85-155 cm) is a separate shower that should be split off or the legitimate far body of a genuinely 2.5 GeV shower, so beyond 14003 I named no further marks. Note also that 113237 (pdg 13, 53.5 cm) sits at dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 on the vertex and is correctly left grey - the reconstruction did keep one vertex track out, it took a different one. Second object worth a line: shw 83070 is a SINGLE 13.2 cm segment tagged pdg 2212 carrying kine_best 135.0 MeV and is listed as a shower; that is a PID question I am not resolving. PI0: the reconstruction accepted group 0 = 113236 + 75062, stored mass 149.3 MeV, from a 2498.2 + 109.5 MeV pair at 18.6 deg (asymmetry 0.92). Since 113236's energy is inflated by exactly the material I am calling over-clustered, that mass is not trustworthy and I dispute the pairing on those grounds without proposing a replacement - 75062 is 160-185 cm out and nearly collinear with 113236, which is what you would expect if the two are pieces of ONE forward EM system rather than two photons from a pi0. Clustering statement, silent on PID except where said. NOT LOOKED AT: the 15 showers the scope rule skipped, all under 20 MeV min_kine_best; of the 6 in scope I opened frames for 113236 only and read 75062, 83070, 67054, 62049, 121231 off the candidate table. This verdict is a claim about 113236.
